prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1166; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a rear-end collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck from behind at a traffic light. The claimant reports a back strain and is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene. The responding officer's notes match the account given by the other driver.

Entry 4: Witness statements and scene photographs were received. Both witnesses describe the impact in the same sequence the other driver described, and the photos show damage consistent with that account.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle damage. The location and severity of the crush line fit the reported impact, and no prior damage to the vehicle is known from the claim history or the appraiser's notes.

Entry 6: Spoke with the claimant's counsel about the injury. The reported back strain fits the kind and force of a rear-end impact, and the claimant has told the same account of the collision in every conversation so far.

Entry 7: Requested prior medical records from the claimant's providers. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from the claimant's history or the records received to date.

Entry 8: Reviewed treatment records. The care followed a usual course of physical therapy and follow-up visits, and the frequency of visits tapered as the claimant's reported symptoms improved.

Entry 9: Received the latest treatment update through counsel. The claimant is progressing, and the remaining care appears to be consistent with the expected recovery timeline for this type of injury.

Entry 10: Reviewed the full file with the other evidence in hand. Liability, injury, and vehicle damage all line up with the reported collision, and the claim is being prepared for evaluation on that basis.
